title: rust-codemap trace event line
description: One JSON-Lines record for a plain tracing::event!/info!/warn!/... call made from directly inside an instrumented function's own body -- NOT a span lifecycle event (see trace-entry.schema.json/trace-close.schema.json for those). Optional: only appears at all if the target code actually calls event!/info!/etc. from inside a #[instrument]'d function; the mandated main() snippet doesn't need to change to produce these, tracing_subscriber already emits them under the exact same JSON formatter. See trace_log.py's own module docstring for how this is told apart from an entry/close line (by `fields.message`, never by `span.name` -- an event's own `span` reports its ENCLOSING span's identity, not one of its own, so it's indistinguishable from a genuine NEW by name alone). See trace-entry.schema.json's own description for why there is no 'formatVersion' field.

fields.description: The event's own message plus whatever fields the event!/info!/... call captured (e.g. {"step": 0, "total": 0} for `tracing::info!(step, total, "running total after this step")`). `message` is the only field ANY event is guaranteed to have (tracing_subscriber always includes it, empty string if the call had no literal message text) -- everything else is call-site-specific and therefore unconstrained here. Never `"new"` or `"close"` -- a fields.message of exactly one of those two values means this line is actually an entry/close event, not an EVENT one; see trace-entry.schema.json / trace-close.schema.json instead.

filename.description: Where the event!/info!/... call itself is written -- NOT the enclosing span's own #[instrument] line (that's `span.line_number`'s job on entry/close lines; here it's this event's own source position).

span.description: The ENCLOSING span's own identity and current fields at the moment this event fired -- NOT a new span identity of the event's own (an event isn't a span at all). trace_log.py attaches this event to whichever span is currently innermost on its own internally-tracked open-span stack, not by reading this object's `name` (which, being the enclosing span's, would be ambiguous the exact same way two crates' identically-named default-instrumented spans already are elsewhere in this format).

spans.description: Unlike an entry/close line's own `spans` (ancestors ONLY, excluding itself), an event's `spans` includes the span it's nested in -- confirmed empirically, not assumed. Not read by trace_log.py for attribution either way (see `span` above).
